Tenancy Agreement Drafting

Custom drafting of a legally sound lease agreement for residential, commercial, furnished, or month-to-month rentals — fully compliant with Act 220 and L.I. 369.

Why You Need This Service

A template lease might not fit your exact situation. What if your property is furnished? What if it's commercial with special terms? What if you need unique provisions for your specific tenant?

A custom lease removes ambiguity. You get:

  • Language tailored to your specific property and situation
  • Terms that actually protect your interests
  • Compliance with Act 220 without compromising landlord rights
  • Clear, plain language your tenant understands
  • A document you can confidently use and defend

What We Draft

  • Residential Lease: Unfurnished apartment or house
  • Furnished Lease: With inventory and condition clauses
  • Commercial Lease: Shop, office, or business premise
  • Month-to-Month Agreement: For flexible short-term rentals
  • Service Lease: Where landlord provides utilities or services
  • Custom Agreements: Any other tenancy arrangement

What's Included

  • Comprehensive Lease: 8–12 page document covering all provisions
  • Rent & Payment Terms: Clear payment schedule and method
  • Termination Clauses: Notice periods under Act 220
  • Maintenance & Repairs: Landlord vs. tenant responsibilities
  • Dispute Procedure: Reference to Rent Control process
  • Annexures: Inventory (if furnished), condition checklist
  • Plain Language: Written so tenants understand their obligations
  • Two Copies: One for you, one for tenant

When You Need This Service

  • You're renting a property for the first time and need a proper lease
  • You have a special situation (furnished, commercial, service)
  • You want a lease tailored to your specific property
  • You've had disputes and want a stronger agreement
  • You're setting up a portfolio and want consistency

Template vs. Custom

A template costs less but may not fit your situation. A custom lease is tailored to you and your property, covers edge cases, and reflects your specific terms. It's the difference between a generic solution and one that actually works for your situation.
